method: Static PE extraction, rizin analysis and Capstone disassembly; cleave facts and atomscan before/after. No specimen was executed. Submitted reputation and filenames were not used to infer behavior.

samples.identification: Modified XMRig self-replicator carrying a Go downloader and Cobalt Strike Beacon
evidence: Native entry path calls 0x14002add4 from 0x14009a2c3. It reads argv[0], takes two footer counters at 0x14002aee5, writes copies under Windows/System and launches them with CreateProcessW at 0x14002b01d. Each clone gets a decremented generation counter; the loop increments at 0x14002b023. This is executable recursive replication, not a constant or API-name inference.
XMRig RTTI includes App, Miner, CpuBackend and DonateStrategy. Native mining configuration selects cn/r and a pool at 3.120.209.58:8080. Mining and zero donation alone are not the hostile basis.

Embedded PE at 0xfc400 is Go. main.main (0x58ed20) checks admin status, downloads an S3 ZIP with net/http.Get through main.GetArchive, extracts to C:/G DATA Security Software/, and calls exec.Command/Run for AVK.exe. Its non-admin path constructs a PowerShell Start-Process request. The G DATA path is a masquerading clue, not a rule requirement.

Embedded PE at 0x5b8601 exports _ReflectiveLoader@4. Code at 0x10009643 XORs the 4096-byte configuration at VA 0x10031028 with 0x69, then parses typed records. Decoded records set port 443, sleep 5000 ms, endpoints ns7/ns8/ns9.softline.top, GET/POST profiles with an Amazon Host header, and rundll32 spawn paths. WinInet request and remote-process execution implementations occur in code. Presence of the embedded DLL does not prove its activation by the outer program.
false_positives: Go reflection data at extracted offset 0x1970d3 contains DeleteValue among unrelated member names; no CLR RegistryKey binding exists.
Go pclntab data at extracted offset 0x24f8e1 contains 0f010d bytes; no SIDT instruction/read sequence exists there.
Go type-table data at extracted offset 0x26a215 contains c9030001 across fields; no multiplication instruction or API hashing exists there.

samples.identification: Gh0st-lineage RAT installer with NtHook rootkit and boot-hook code
evidence: Outer PE stages a driver, writes its ImagePath, enables SeLoadDriverPrivilege at 0x40251d and calls the dynamically resolved ZwLoadDriver pointer at 0x402537. It then opens the NtHook device. The version resource asks the user to allow execution while the payload supplies remote surveillance.

Embedded kernel PE at 0xba50 imports KeServiceDescriptorTable and installs syscall interception. Its directory-query handler compacts linked directory results to remove selected records. It also embeds a second driver and the safemon.dll RAT, with code to write safemon.dll at 0x15829.

Driver boot code saves/replaces the INT 13h vector at file offset 0x6c0c and patches read boot-code buffers with CALL FAR at 0x6cfe. The kernel disk routine copies this bootstrap at 0x132e5 and invokes the disk write helper at 0x1332f. This supports boot-hook payload code, not a separate generic claim that arbitrary driver-load APIs load that payload.

Embedded safemon.dll at 0x147d8 has Gh0st manager RTTI. Polling loop at 0x1000e290 sleeps, checks GetAsyncKeyState high bits at 0x1000e366 and formats key records with foreground-window context. Writer at 0x1000e050 XORs records with 0x62 at 0x1000e133 before its file-write handoff at 0x1000e14f. Clipboard routine at 0x10010a30 resolves OpenClipboard/GetClipboardData and copies CF_TEXT into a tagged record. These are implemented surveillance paths, not ordinary hotkey imports.

samples.identification: StormAttack DLL injector/persistence installer with erased resource payload
evidence: DLL injection at 0x401150 uses CreateProcessA, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, resolves LoadLibraryA and passes it to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.

Persistence routine at 0x401260 deletes and rewrites the LanmanServer ServiceDLL value with its own DLL path (RegSetValueExA at 0x40133e). Active Setup routine at 0x401900 creates a GUID component, writes StubPath at 0x401a4b, reads its own file and patches/writes a clone at 0x401b26.
Self-delete routine 0x401390 gets its own short path, constructs COMSPEC /c del and starts it via CreateProcessA at 0x4014b8.

StormServer.dll identity and Storm ddos Server banners corroborate the distinctive injector. The entire .rsrc is zero-filled; FindResourceA failure at 0x40249d returns false. A usable DLL drop or active DDoS engine is not established for these bytes. Existing descriptions already distinguish retained code/API profiles from successful installation.
